item.text: {"reviews":[{"benchmark":"arc","instrument_review":"ARC-AGI-2 provides a focused comparison of AI performance on unfamiliar coloured-grid problems, provided prior exposure and testing conditions are considered. Worked examples and exact output matching make the task and credit rule clear. Human difficulty studies and checks for repeated solution rules support test construction, but matching difficulty for people does not establish equivalent difficulty for AI. Scores average the fraction of new inputs solved within each problem; they should not be reported as the percentage of problems fully solved. Exact matching gives a clear success criterion but does not distinguish nearly correct grids from entirely wrong ones. Verified settings and spending limits help comparisons, while single runs and missing repeatability estimates leave small score differences uncertain. Public materials and dated corrections support inspection, although comparisons must account for revisions and testing routes. The supplied evidence supports conclusions about grid-task performance, with broader reasoning and intelligence claims remaining unresolved.","supported_claims":["The benchmark tests whether AI systems can infer rules from examples and produce correct outputs on two-dimensional grid tasks.","The inspected software allows two attempts per new input, requires an exact match, and averages within-problem fractions across problems.","Developers used human solving results to select test sets with similar difficulty for people and reviewed puzzles for repeated solution rules.","Verified evaluations specify settings and spending limits; public problems, software, marking tests and dated corrections enable inspection."],"documented_problems":["Public evaluation problems can be seen in advance, complicating claims that they are unfamiliar to a tested system.","The change record documents corrections to coloured squares and unclear examples, but affected AI scores are not all recalculated.","The software's fractional problem scores can be confused with the dataset's stricter definition of a fully solved problem.","Verified evaluations use one run, limiting what an individual result reveals about consistency."],"missing_information":["Repeated identical-test results and uncertainty estimates for AI scores.","Systematic evidence about sensitivity to instructions, grid presentation and software changes.","Evidence establishing equivalence of test-set difficulty for AI systems.","Evidence ruling out unintended routes to high scores and establishing each system's relevant prior exposure.","Studies connecting scores to language, social interaction, real-world work or broader intelligence; independent verification of the complete marking system and reporting archive."],"reinterpretations":["For AI, a high score means successful grid outputs under particular settings, attempts and resource limits; it does not by itself establish a particular internal reasoning process.","Human difficulty matching supplies a construction reference, rather than a measure of AI stability or AI difficulty equivalence.","A reported score represents average within-problem input success, rather than necessarily the proportion of whole problems solved.","Broader human-like reasoning claims require evidence beyond success on the supplied grid tasks."],"closing_note":"The instructions are clear. Any reported comparison should identify the test set, revision, testing route and meaning of the score."},{"benchmark":"designqa","instrument_review":"DesignQA offers a useful examination of AI performance on specified engineering-document and vehicle-image tasks. Real competition materials and practitioner contributions support relevance to those tasks, but one rulebook and six unevenly sized groups provide limited coverage of engineering work. Question review adds some quality control, although its exceptions and unreported disagreement leave answer quality uncertain. Marking can penalize formatting differences or valid answers missing from the reference, so credit partly reflects agreement with supplied wording. Equal weighting gives each group the same influence despite differing sizes and marking methods; the overall score therefore needs explanation alongside group results. Comparisons also reflect how information is supplied, since systems receive different rulebook access. Limited consistency evidence and very small groups weaken close rankings. Public materials permit partial inspection, but incomplete historical records hinder full reproduction. Scores support conclusions about these tasks under stated conditions, rather than established competence on other engineering documents or projects.","supported_claims":["The benchmark contains 1,451 question-and-answer pairs across six groups covering rule finding, terminology, component recognition, dimensions and performance requirements.","Real Formula SAE rules, designs and test data give the questions a practical engineering connection.","The paper describes tested systems, instructions, settings, comparison baselines and several changes to supplied information or images.","Public questions, scoring code, instructions and some AI responses support inspection of parts of the evaluation."],"documented_problems":["Coverage is restricted to one rulebook and limited task types; group sizes range from 1,192 individual-rule questions to 16 performance questions.","Wording and formatting affect credit, including missing commas and valid related rules absent from reference answers.","Systems receive different information supplies, so reported differences combine AI performance with document-access or retrieval effects.","All described scale-bar drawings comply with the rule, allowing an always-yes answer to earn the decision credit on that portion; this does not establish that any AI used that strategy.","The released materials do not fully link historical code, settings and inputs to every result, and one answer file has fewer rows than the corresponding question count."],"missing_information":["Reviewer disagreement rates, remaining answer errors and comprehensive evidence of marking accuracy and consistency.","Evidence that group scores or the equally weighted overall score measure distinct underlying skills.","Identical-condition repeat runs and uncertainty estimates sufficient to interpret small model differences.","A human-engineer baseline and evidence that performance transfers to other technical documents or real projects.","Systematic exposure checks, a protected test set and clear rules for training on questions or repeated submissions.","A clear account of revision effects on scores, a licence file and complete reuse rules in the inspected materials."],"reinterpretations":["For AI, results describe the system together with its supplied passages, images and retrieval arrangement.","Text-similarity credit reflects agreement with reference wording as well as the engineering content of an answer.","The overall score gives equal influence to six task groups; it does not represent accuracy across all questions or established general engineering competence.","Correct yes/no decisions on the described compliant scale-bar drawings cannot alone demonstrate that an AI checked the requirement."],"closing_note":"The review instructions are clear. Reports should specify information access, scoring version and group results; reuse permissions remain unclear in the inspected materials."}]}
